question: Can we predict a machine’s bounded-time outcome using much less memory?
idea: For the specified one-writable-tape machines, the manuscript claims a simulation using roughly T to the two-fifths power in space, with logarithmic factors, to determine the outcome by time T. Its running time is unrestricted. The time cutoff matters: this does not decide whether a machine will ever halt.
why: The mathematics of computation: what algorithms can do, how much work they need, and which problems are hard to solve.
exactClaim: Determines the halting and finite-control outcome of a fixed deterministic one-writable-tape machine up to time T using $O(T^{2/5}\log^C(T+2))$ space, improving the square-root exponent. Heads move at most one cell per step; finitely many read-only input heads are allowed. Initial contents are independent of T, and contents and input symbols have polylogarithmic-space access. Simulation time is unrestricted.
reviewStatus: assistant-authored from source summary; not mathematically reviewed
scope: Family-level introduction based on the pinned catalogue summary. Summarizes manuscript claims; not an independent proof review.
